source: High Country Fly Fishing Guides and Locals

conditions.overall: Fishing has been wonderful the last month thanks to consistent rainfall keeping wild creek water levels great. The Watauga has been excellent with feeder streams adding extra water, while the South Holston is running high with 24/7 generation as Holston Lake approaches full pool.

top_flies.name: Chubby Chernobyl
top_flies.note: Wild water WNC recommendation. Also listed for South Holston at #12-14.

top_flies.name: Frenchies
top_flies.note: Wild water WNC recommendation. Also listed for Watauga at #18-20.

top_flies.name: Squirmy Worm
top_flies.note: Wild water WNC — recommended for stained water conditions.

top_flies.name: Pat's Rubber Leg
top_flies.note: Wild water WNC — recommended for stained water. Also listed for Watauga at #12-14.

top_flies.name: Caddis Dry
top_flies.note: Watauga River — below the Doe there is a lot of caddis activity.

top_flies.name: Zebra Midge
top_flies.note: Watauga River recommendation (above the Doe: small midges, baetis, scuds). Also listed for South Holston at #18-22.

top_flies.name: Baetis Nymph
top_flies.note: Watauga River — above the Doe it's normal summer bugs (small midges, baetis, scuds).

top_flies.name: Sulphur Dry
top_flies.note: South Holston — sulphur hatches occurring during generations.

tactics: On the Watauga, an hour-long pulse occurs in the AM (normally 6–7 AM), followed by normal recreational flow beginning at 1 PM — time your fishing accordingly.
Above the Doe on the Watauga, focus on small midges, baetis, and scuds. Below the Doe, there is a lot of caddis activity.
On the South Holston, pay attention to release schedules — as of now the dam is running 24/7 but these conditions can change at the drop of a hat.
On wild WNC streams, if you get a big rain event the night before, have a couple of streams in mind in case one of them is muddy.
Off color water doesn't automatically mean don't fish it — there is a big difference between blown out muddy and off color. Some of the best fishing this summer has been in off color water.
Light dry droppers with small dries has been the name of the game on wild water.
No stocking will occur in any delayed harvest streams until October — fishing is solely on wild streams in the WNC area.

waters.name: Watauga River
waters.note: Fishing has been excellent. Feeder streams (Doe and Stoney Creek) have been pumping in extra water for at least a month, keeping fish happy and feeding well. Above the Doe: small midges, baetis, scuds. Below the Doe: lots of caddis activity. Watch for the AM pulse (6–7 AM) and normal rec flow starting at 1 PM.

waters.name: Doe Creek (Watauga feeder)
waters.note: One of the feeder streams contributing extra water to the Watauga River for at least a month. Used as a reference point for fly selection — above vs. below the Doe.

waters.name: Stoney Creek (Watauga feeder)
waters.note: One of the feeder streams pumping extra water into the Watauga River for at least a month.

waters.name: South Holston River
waters.note: With Holston Lake getting near full pool, more generation has started. Sulphur hatches occurring during generations. Currently running 24/7 for the foreseeable future, but conditions can change without notice — always check release schedules.

waters.name: Wild Streams (Western North Carolina)
waters.note: Water levels have been great with consistent rainfall. Some mornings a drive-around is needed to find clear water after a big rain event. No stocking in any delayed harvest streams until October — fishing is entirely on wild fish.

elevation_note: High Country streams (Boone, 3300-4000ft) run 1-2 weeks behind lower-elevation WNC
stocking_note: No stocking will occur in any delayed harvest streams until October.
